Costs & Insurance

Does Homeowners Insurance Cover Slab Leaks in Florida?

By SRQ Leak Pros Editorial · Published November 4, 2026 · Updated November 5, 2026 · 5 min read

Short answer: Homeowners insurance often covers some slab leak costs, but rarely all. Many policies pay to access the pipe and repair sudden water damage, while excluding the pipe repair itself and leaks that ran for a long time. In Florida, notice of a property claim is due within 1 year after the date of loss, under § 627.70132.

Finding out you have a slab leak is bad enough. Then comes the next question: will insurance help? The honest answer is "it depends on your policy." This guide explains what policies commonly cover, what they often exclude and how to protect your claim. If you need the leak found first, SRQ Leak Pros can connect you with a local pro for slab leak repair in Sarasota.

This is general information, not legal or insurance advice. Every policy differs. Read yours and talk with your agent.

Does homeowners insurance cover slab leaks?

Most policies split a slab leak into three parts, and each part is treated differently.

Part of the lossOften covered?Why
Finding and reaching the pipe (tear-out)Often, in many policiesSome policies pay to access the leak
Fixing the pipe itselfOften notWear and tear is a common exclusion
Water damage to floors, walls and contentsOften, if suddenSudden and accidental damage is a common covered loss
Damage from a slow leak over monthsOften notMany policies exclude repeated or long-term seepage
Mold from the leakLimitedMany policies cap or exclude mold
Foundation damageVariesDepends on cause and exclusions

Look for the words "access," "tear-out," "sudden and accidental," "continuous or repeated seepage," "wear and tear" and "mold" in your policy.

Why "sudden" vs. "slow" matters

Insurers often cover damage that happens suddenly. A pipe that bursts and floods a room is a clear example. A pinhole leak that seeped for months is harder. Many policies exclude water damage that happened over a long time. That is why early detection matters for both your home and your claim.

The EPA's simple meter test can catch a slow leak early: read your meter, use no water for two hours, then read it again.

Florida claim deadlines

Florida Statutes § 627.70132 sets the notice deadlines for property insurance claims:

  • Initial or reopened claim: notice within 1 year after the date of loss
  • Supplemental claim: notice within 18 months after the date of loss

Don't wait to report. Many policies also require "prompt" notice and steps to prevent more damage.

How to protect your slab leak claim

  1. Stop the water. Close the main shut-off or the branch valve. Policies often require you to prevent further damage.
  2. Take photos and video. Capture wet floors, stains, the meter moving and any visible damage.
  3. Get the leak located in writing. A detection report showing the location and cause helps the adjuster.
  4. Call your insurer or agent. Ask what is covered and whether they need to inspect before repairs.
  5. Keep every receipt. Detection, repairs, drying, hotel stays and replaced items.
  6. Don't throw out damaged materials until the insurer says it's OK, or photograph them well.
  7. Ask about a reroute. If the policy pays tear-out but not the pipe, the repair method can change what's covered.

What a detection report should show

  • Date and time of testing
  • Meter readings before and after
  • Which line leaks: hot or cold, and which branch
  • The marked location of the leak
  • The method used: pressure, acoustic, thermal or tracer gas
  • Photos of the moisture readings
  • The likely cause, if it can be seen
  • The provider's Florida plumbing contractor license number

What a slab leak costs if insurance won't pay

Angi's national data puts the average slab leak repair at about $2,300, with detection averaging about $280. That's before water damage cleanup and flooring. See slab leak repair cost for the full breakdown.

Do home warranties cover slab leaks?

Some home warranty plans cover certain plumbing repairs, but slab leaks are often limited or excluded. A home warranty is a service contract, not insurance. Read the contract for slab leak terms, caps and access costs.

Sarasota homes and slab leak claims

Most Sarasota homes are built on concrete slabs, so slab leaks are a common claim type here. Seasonal owners face an extra risk: a leak that starts while the home is empty can run long enough to be called "continuous or repeated." Some policies also limit coverage for homes left vacant. Close the main shut-off when you leave, and have someone check the meter.

How to prevent slab leak damage

  • Read the meter monthly and after any trip.
  • Install a pressure reducing valve if pressure is high.
  • Consider a leak sensor or automatic shut-off valve.
  • Watch for warm spots and damp baseboards.
  • Fix the first leak quickly, and ask whether more are likely.

Local note: seasonal homes on Longboat Key and Siesta Key should close the main before long trips. Older slab homes in Venice often have aging copper, so a meter check after storms is wise.

  • Your insurer asks for a leak detection report

Frequently asked questions

Will insurance pay to break up my floor to reach a slab leak?

Many policies include tear-out or access coverage, but not all. Check your policy wording and ask your agent before work begins.

Is a slab leak considered sudden?

It depends on how long it ran and how your policy defines covered water damage. Slow leaks over months are often excluded.

How long do I have to report a slab leak claim in Florida?

Under § 627.70132, notice of an initial claim is due within 1 year after the date of loss, and a supplemental claim within 18 months.

Should I call the insurer or the plumber first?

Stop the water first. Then get the leak located and call your insurer promptly. Ask whether they need to inspect before repairs.
